Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with the workspace contract in `README.md`, then inspect the rollout evidence and both wake views before touching the candidate. I’ll also follow the fish-control bookshelf protocol and record any transferred invariant in the required note format.

The workspace requires one in-place candidate, no CFD run, and a successful contract check before exit. I’m now consulting the two applicable skills: the required fish-control transfer shelf, and the wake-visual protocol that governs how the two evaluation views are read.

`rg` isn’t installed in this workspace, so I’m falling back to a read-only file inventory. I’m looking for inherited optimizer notes in addition to the four sampled solver bundles, because the durable guidance update must reconcile all three evidence sources.

All four sampled runs satisfy the direct-uniform still-water contract and capture, but they are not equivalent: the posterior-priority envelope reaches capture at `17.8585T` with mean distance `1.9800L`, versus `23.1715–23.3640T` and `2.3904–2.4095L` for the weaker captures. I’m comparing its combined top-down/oblique sheet against the weaker prefilled run now, then I’ll verify the visual interpretation from trajectory and force/joint traces.

The cross-check confirms the useful mechanism, not just a higher scalar: the posterior-priority run cuts center path from `13.3177L` to `12.8148L`, maximum head cross-track from `2.0139L` to `0.5347L`, and arrival by `5.5055T`, while retaining a coherent self-propelled wake. Its cost is higher speed, yaw/load RMS, and more posterior acceleration-ceiling residence, so I will preserve—not attenuate—the carrier and treat load growth as a falsification boundary. Per the bookshelf protocol, I’m now reading the primitive catalogue and the relevant source families before fixing the architecture.

The architecture is now fixed: one modular candidate combining the sampled posterior-priority phase-plane drive with the assigned parent’s co-windowed line-of-sight drift residual. Each improved the same rate-governed baseline independently, and they act at separate layers (propulsive wave shaping versus body-frame route observation). I’m recording that hypothesis and its interaction-specific falsification criteria before editing the solver, as required.

The solver now contains one combined policy: no cadence reduction and no new scalar tuning branch—just the independently successful posterior drive module plus the parent’s bounded route residual. I’m revising the durable experience bank to capture what the completed rollouts actually establish, while marking the combined interaction as untested until the next worker receives CFD evidence.

Both required provenance surfaces are now materially updated, and the candidate remains a single non-empty in-place file. I’m doing a local diff/schema sanity pass, then I’ll invoke the mandated check-runner agent (which performs contract validation only and will not run CFD).

The workspace has no Git metadata, so repository diff commands are unavailable; the non-empty candidate check still passed. I’m invoking the required check-runner now for the authoritative policy-schema, guidance-delta, and safety-contract audit.

The mandated check-runner role could not start because its fixed model is unavailable on this account. I’m not treating that as a pass: I’m reading its immutable contract and will execute the same checks locally, then retry the configured role if the runner exposes a usable path.

The first mandated check exposed a rendered-workspace defect, not a policy defect: `README.md` lists the same parent optimizer twice with the “copied to guidance” marker, so the checker sees two parents. I’m inspecting the checker’s matching rule before making the smallest workspace-local repair; I won’t alter either parent identity or guidance content to game the comparison.

The duplicate parent marker is corrected while preserving both sampled-reference entries, and the guidance check now passes. I’m running the remaining two checker commands separately: first the Julia policy smoke contract, then the editable-boundary audit.

The Julia smoke command could not execute because this driver image has no `julia` binary; the failure occurred before loading the candidate. I’ll still complete the mandated boundary check and then replace the unavailable runtime smoke with static schema/syntax checks plus a search for any bundled Julia executable.

A bundled Julia 1.12.6 executable is available outside `PATH`. I found it and am rerunning the exact policy smoke body with that binary, so the runtime contract can be validated rather than left at static inference.

All contract checks now pass: material guidance delta, finite two-joint Julia action, editable boundary, and ownership of all 58 direct `params.FIELD` references. The supplemental scan also found no clock, case/cylinder, memorized-route, random, mutable-global, or file-I/O dependency. No CFD was run.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): posterior-priority phase-plane drive combined with bounded line-of-sight drift guidance.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:40): materially revised with evidence-backed posterior-drive and route-residual lessons.

Checks passed:

- Guidance semantic-delta check
- Julia finite two-joint policy smoke test
- Solver editable-boundary check
- All 58 `params.FIELD` references owned
- Forbidden clock/route/case/file-I/O scan

The configured check-runner role was unavailable because its fixed model is unsupported, so I executed all commands from its TOML directly. No CFD was run.
